Website= folder of .html files plus a computer thats always on
Quartos going to write your .html 
You write .qmd files and then quarto the machine converts to .html
Quarto reads the file from top to bottom, finds code chunks, and sends them to R to get results back, then glues text results into html.
If theres errors in the code chunks wont be able to change them to html
In R studio you can use about .qmd to get the template

Anatomy of .qmd:
YAML
Code chunks

“(R)

2+2
“

Git/Github/Github Desktop:

Github desktop= buttons that tell git what to do
“COMMIT” → “save a labele snapshot” - lives on your computer
Commiting and saving are not the same thing, when you click commit on github you can forever see all the changes you made in your code
“PUSH” → “send my screenshot to GitHub.com”
Makes your changes public

## Key Concepts

Three places a file can live:

1. **My computer** — where I edit
2. **GitHub.com** — where it's stored
3. **My live site** — what the world sees

The loop: **Edit → Save → Render → Commit → Push → wait → refresh**

## Proving R Works

The chunk below runs when this page renders. If you can see a result underneath
it on your published site, R and Quarto are talking to each other correctly.

```{r}
sessionInfo()$R.version$version.string
```
